w1031-03-mirror-mint.vo: Mint and rye bread get their smell from mirror image molecules. Take the spearmint in his hand. Its smell is a molecule called carvone. And the rye bread's smell comes from the caraway seeds baked into it, which are full of carvone too. Same atoms. Same bonds. But one is FLIPPED, like his left hand and his right. Lay one on the other, and no matter how he turns it, it never lines up. Chemists call that kyral. [curious] So how does his nose tell them apart? The smell receptors inside it are kyral too, so each version fits them differently. One smells like mint... and its mirror image, like rye bread. Free practice for this on levlprep dot com.
